I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. A few years ago, I was renting a place with this dude. We were on a lease, and when the lease was ending, he just left without giving much notice. He took most of his stuff, leaving only the last bit of his half of the rent and a few things he didn't want to bring with him. There was a note saying he didn't want those things. Now, where I live, if you don't get rid of your stuff when you move out, the landlord can pay someone to remove it, and it's a rip-off. I've heard of people losing $250 from their deposit just because someone had to take three milk crates of stuff to the dump. So, I texted and emailed him for two weeks asking him to pick up his stuff or let me take them to the dump, but he never responded. So, I took most of his stuff to the dump, but he had around 60 video games for the PS4. I figured I'd sell them. There's a local game store that buys used games, and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Now, last week, I was at a party where he was, and we were being polite. He asked how the move-out was, and I said it was good. Naturally, he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games. I told him I tried to get him to grab those things, but he never reached out. Now he's calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked, and legally, there's nothing wrong with what I did, but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this. Okay, so to figure this out, I need to think about the situation from different angles. First, what were the terms of the lease? Did it specify what happens to belongings left behind? If the lease says that the landlord can dispose of items, then legally, I was in the right to get rid of his stuff. But emotionally, is it right to sell someone's games without their consent? Even if legally it's okay, is it morally justifiable? Did I make an effort to contact him? I did text and email him for two weeks, but he didn't respond. So, I tried to give him a chance to retrieve his stuff. But selling his games for $600 seems like a significant amount. Did I consider that these games might have sentimental value to him? Or maybe he still wanted them? I mean, I sold them for money, but is that the right thing to do? Also, by selling his games, I'm depriving him of his property, even if he didn't respond to my attempts to contact him. Is there a better way to handle this situation? Maybe donating the games or holding onto them longer? But then, the landlord was going to charge him for removal, which would have come out of his deposit. So, by taking the games to the dump, I saved him from losing money. But selling them for $600 seems like I'm profiting from his stuff. Is it fair to sell someone's property when they're not responding to your attempts to contact them? Or should I have held onto the games longer or found another way to dispose of them without selling? Also, how does this affect our relationship? He's now calling me an asshole, which is hurtful. Did I consider how he would feel when I sold his games? Or did I just think about the legal and financial aspects? Maybe I should have been more empathetic and tried harder to reach him before selling his stuff. Or perhaps I should have given him a heads-up that I was going to sell the games if he didn't respond. But legally, I was in the clear, so is it wrong to take advantage of that? Or is it still not the right thing to do because it affects our relationship negatively? I'm also thinking about the value of the games. $600 is a lot for used games. Did I get a fair price? Or did I take advantage of the store's willingness to buy used games? Overall, I'm torn between doing what's legally right and what's morally or emotionally right. I don't want to be seen as an asshole, but I also don't want to lose money or deal with the hassle of someone else's stuff. Maybe I should have found a middle ground, like donating the games or holding onto them longer. Or perhaps I should have given him a portion of the money from selling them, even though legally I wasn't obligated to. But then, if I give him money, that would be admitting some fault, which I don't think I did. I followed the lease terms and tried to contact him. So, legally, I'm in the right, but morally, is there a gray area? I guess I need to consider the impact of my actions on our relationship and whether the money I made is worth the friendship or goodwill I might have lost. In the end, I think I did what was necessary to protect myself financially and legally, but maybe I could have handled it in a way that was more considerate of his feelings. That way, I wouldn't be seen as the asshole, but also wouldn't have to deal with the negative consequences of our falling out.
